## Clarifier — All clear

`kind: infra` workflow-fix task, body fully specifies the gap, the incident
evidence (#1491 inline-override round, 2026-08-05T05:44Z), and the two candidate
edit sites (CLAUDE.md § "Explicit user inline override" / its parent
"Detached-by-default + lifecycle ack" sub-block; `.claude/skills/issue/SKILL.md`
Step 9a-ter canonical blocks). No blocking ambiguity for the user.

**One design concern carried to the planner (not a user question).** Grounded
pre-plan probe: `tick_triage.ISSUE_TERMINAL` =
`{completed, archived, awaiting_promotion, blocked, on_hold}` returns
`TERMINAL` / `GATE-TRANSITION`, and both verdicts run CRON-TEARDOWN and END THE
TURN (`.claude/skills/issue-tick/SKILL.md` verdict table). #1491 sits at
`awaiting_promotion`. So the change AS LITERALLY WORDED in the body ("arm the
45-min `/issue-tick <N>` cron at dispatch exactly as Step 0/6d.2 sessions do")
would, on the actual incident, have fired once within ~45-50 min, emitted one
MISLEADING phone push ("parked at awaiting_promotion — open it", while a
~$44/h pod round was live), and then DELETED ITSELF — zero ongoing survival
coverage, plus a false sense of one. Inline/override rounds normally run on
exactly these park/terminal-status parents, so this is the dominant case, not
an edge.

The plan therefore delivers the task's INTENT (a real session-survival backstop
for inline/override rounds that dispatch work outliving the turn) with a
status-conditional mechanism, rather than the literal instruction. Assumption
stated in plan §1; the critic is the check on it.

No clarifying questions. Advancing to `planning`.

   tuple; `tests/test_select_step9c_tests.py` pins tuple-manifest

   `--map-files` arms are WORKFLOW_INVARIANT-EXCLUDED by design, so a
   registered invariant pin can never appear there (confirmed: 0 hits).
   Registration is instead proven by pin 4 (tuple membership), the 153
   selector self-tests (tuple-manifest-tree parity), and the selector
   `--json` (`reason: invariant`, `missing_invariants=[]`).

   appears" disjunction is vacuous once the class names appear. Implemented
   per-class set-EQUALITY instead: regex-extract each class's backticked
   enumeration from the block, assert equality against
